text:
When  the switch  S, in the circuit shown, is closed, then the value of current i will be : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]

We start by applying Kirchhoff's current law at point C in the circuit:

$i_{1}+i_{2}=i$

where $i_{1}$ and $i_{2}$ are the currents flowing through resistors $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ respectively, and i is the current flowing through the battery and resistor $R_{3}$.

Next, we use Ohm's law to express $i_{1}$ and $i_{2}$ in terms of the voltages at points A, B, and C:

$i_{1}=\frac{V_{A}-V_{C}}{R_{1}}=\frac{20-V_{C}}{2}$

$i_{2}=\frac{V_{B}-V_{C}}{R_{2}}=\frac{10-V_{C}}{4}$

where $R_{1}$ and $R_{2}$ are the resistances of resistors R1 and R2 respectively.

Substituting these expressions into the first equation, we get:

$\frac{20-V_{C}}{2}+\frac{10-V_{C}}{4}=i$

We then use Ohm's law again to express i in terms of the voltages at points C and earth :

$i=\frac{V_{C}-V}{R_{3}}=\frac{V_{C}-0}{2}=\frac{V_{C}}{2}$

Substituting this expression into the previous equation, we get:

$\frac{20-V_{C}}{2}+\frac{10-V_{C}}{4}=\frac{V_{C}}{2}$

Simplifying this equation, we get:

$40-2V_{C}+10-V_{C}=2V_{C}$

$50=5V_{C}$

$V_{C}=10\text{V}$

Finally, we use Ohm's law to find the value of the current i:

$i=\frac{V_{C}}{2}=\frac{10}{2}=5\text{A}$

Therefore, the current flowing through the circuit is 5 A.

text: Two coherent sources produce waves of different intensities which interfere. After interference, the ratio of the maximum intensity to the minimum intensity is 16. The intensity of the waves are in the ratio :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given that, 

$\frac{\mathrm{I}_{\max }}{\mathrm{I}_{\min }}=\frac{16}{1}$

We  know, 

$I_{\max }$ $=$ $\left (\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}\right )^{2}$

and $I_{\min }$ $=\left (\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}\right )^{2}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{\left (\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}\right )^{2}}{\left (\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}\right )^{2}}=\frac{16}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}-\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}}=\frac{4}{1}$

$\Rightarrow$   $4\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}-4\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}+\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$   $3\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}=5\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{1}}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{I}_{2}}}=\frac{5}{3}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{\mathrm{I}_{1}}{\mathrm{I}_{2}}=\frac{25}{9}$

text:
Surface of certain metal is first illuminated with light of wavelength $λ_{1}$ = 350 nm and then, by light of wavelength $λ_{2}$ = 540 nm. It is found that the maximum speed of the photo electrons in the two cases differ by a factor of 2. The work function of the metal (in eV) is close to : 

(Energy of photon = $\frac{1240}{λ(innm)}$eV)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let speed of photoelectron in first case is 2v

then in the second case speed is v.

For first case 

$\frac{hc}{λ_{1}}=𝜙+\frac{1}{2}m(2v)^{2}$

For second case,

$\frac{hc}{λ_{2}}=𝜙+\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\therefore$   $\frac{\frac{hc}{λ1}-𝜙}{\frac{hc}{λ2}-𝜙}=\frac{\frac{1}{2}m\times 4v^{2}}{\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{hc}{λ_{1}}-𝜙$ = 4$\left (\frac{hc}{λ_{2}}-𝜙\right )$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{4hc}{λ_{2}}$ $-$ $\frac{hc}{λ_{1}}$ = 3$𝜙$

$\Rightarrow$   $𝜙$ $=$ $\frac{hc}{3}\left (\frac{4}{λ_{2}}-\frac{1}{λ_{1}}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$   $𝜙$ $=$  $\frac{1240}{3}\left (\frac{4}{540}-\frac{1}{350}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$   $𝜙$ = 1.8 eV

text:
Temperature difference of $120^{o}C$ is maintained between ends of a uniform rod AB of length 2L. Another bent rod PQ, of same cross-section as AB and length $\frac{3L}{2},$ is connected across AB  (see figure). In steady state, temperature difference between P and Q will be  close to : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,

Resistance, R = $\frac{ρL}{A}$

$\therefore$   R $\propto$ L

So, Resistance is directly proportional to length of the rod.


[IMG]


Equivalent resistance between A and B is,

$R_{eq} =$  $\frac{R}{2}+\frac{R\times \frac{3R}{2}}{R+\frac{3R}{2}}+\frac{R}{2}$

=  R + $\frac{3R^{2}}{2}\times \frac{2}{5R}$

= R + $\frac{3R}{5}$

= $\frac{8R}{5}$

Thermal current between point A and B is, 

      I = $\frac{\Delta T_{AB}}{\mathrm{R}_{eq}}$

=  $\frac{120-0}{\frac{8R}{5}}$

=   $\frac{120\times 5}{8R}$

Resistance between P and Q = $\frac{3R}{5}$

$\therefore$   $\Delta T_{PQ} =$ $\mathrm{I}\times \frac{3R}{5}$

=  $\frac{120\times 5}{8R}\times \frac{3R}{5}$

$= 45^{o}C$

Consider a tank made of glass(refractive index 1.5) with a thick bottom. It is filled with a liquid of refractive index $μ$. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:

When light is incident on the liquid at $90^{o}$, then from ssnells  law,

$1.\sin 90^{o} =$ $μ$sin$θ$

$\Rightarrow$   sin$θ$ = $\frac{1}{μ}$ . . . . . . (1)

Between liquid and glass, 

$μ$sin$θ$ = 1.5 sin r

$\Rightarrow$   $μ$sin$θ$ $= 1.5 \sin  (90^{o}$ $-$ $θ$)

$\Rightarrow$   $μ$ tan$θ$ = 1.5

$\Rightarrow$   tan$θ$ = $\frac{1.5}{μ}$

$\therefore$   sin$θ$ = $\frac{1.5}{\sqrt{μ^{2}+(1.5)^{2}}}$ . . . . . . (2)

$\therefore$    From (1) and (2) we get, 

$\frac{1}{μ}$ = $\frac{1.5}{\sqrt{μ^{2}+(1.5)^{2}}}$

$\Rightarrow$   $μ^{2}$ $+ (1.5)^{2} =$ $μ^{2}$ $\times$ $(1.5)^{2}$

text: A heavy ball of mass M is suspended from the ceiling of a car by a light string of mass m (m < < M). When the car is at rest, the speed of transverse waves in the string is $60 ms^{-1}$. When the car has acceleration a, the wave-speed increases to $60.5 ms^{-1}$. The value of a, in terms of gravitational acceleration g, is closest to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


Resultant force on the ball of mass M when car is moving with a acceleration a is , 

$F_{$net} = $\sqrt{(Mg)^{2}+(Ma)^{2}}$

   = $M\sqrt{g^{2}+a^{2}}$

$\therefore$   T = M$\sqrt{g^{2}+a^{2}}$

We know, 

Velocity, V = $\sqrt{\frac{T}{μ}}$

When Car is at rest then, 

   60 = $\sqrt{\frac{Mg}{μ}}$   . . . . (1)

and when is moving then 

   60.5 =  $\sqrt{\frac{M\sqrt{g^{2}+a^{2}}}{μ}}$    . . . . (2)

By dividing (2) by (1) we get, 

$\frac{60.5}{60}=\sqrt{\frac{\sqrt{g^{2}+a^{2}}}{g}}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\left (1+\frac{0.5}{60}\right )$ = $\left (\frac{g^{2}+a^{2}}{g^{2}}\right )^{\frac{1}{4}}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{g^{2}+a^{2}}{g^{2}}$ = $\left (1+\frac{0.5}{60}\right )^{4}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{g^{2}+a^{2}}{g^{2}}$ = 1 + 4 $\times$ $\frac{0.5}{60}$ [Using Binomial approximation]

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{g^{2}+a^{2}}{g^{2}}$ = 1 + $\frac{1}{30}$

$\Rightarrow$   1 + $\frac{a^{2}}{g^{2}}$ = 1 + $\frac{1}{30}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{a}{g}$ = $\frac{1}{\sqrt{30}}$

$\Rightarrow$   a = $\frac{g}{\sqrt{30}}$

$\therefore$   Closest answer, a = $\frac{g}{5}$

text:
A block of mass m, lying on a smooth horizontal surface, is attached to a spring (of negligible mass) of spring constant k. The other end of the spring is fixed, as shown in the figure. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


When block is pulled x distance with F force, then it is at maximum speed position

$\therefore$   F = Kx

$\Rightarrow$   x = $\frac{F}{K}$

Applying work energy theorem, work done by all the forces = change in Kinetic energy.

$\Rightarrow$  $W_{$Force$} + W_{$Spring} = $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}-0$

$\Rightarrow$   Fx $-$ $\frac{1}{2}Kx^{2} =$ $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $F\left (\frac{F}{K}\right )-\frac{1}{2}K\left (\frac{F}{K}\right )^{2}$ = $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{F^{2}}{K}-\frac{F{}^{2}}{2K}$ = $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{F{}^{2}}{2K}$ =  $\frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $v$ = $\frac{F}{\sqrt{mK}}$

solution.body:

$\therefore$   $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{1}{2}r^{2}\frac{dθ}{dt}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac{1}{2}r^{2}ω$    . . . . . (1)

We know, 

angular momentum, 

L = $mvr$

=  $m(ωr)r$

$=  mr^{2}ω$

$\therefore$   $ω$ =  $\frac{L}{mr^{2}}$     . . . . . (2)

Put value of $ω$ in equation(1),

$\frac{dA}{dt}$ = $\frac{1}{2}r^{2}$ ($\frac{L}{mr^{2}}$)

=  $\frac{L}{2m}$

text:
Three blocks A, B and C are lying on a smooth horizontal surface, as shown in the figure. A and B have equal masses, m while C has mass M. Block A is given an initial speed $υ$ towards B due to which it collides with B perfectly inelastically. The combined mass collides with C, also perfectly inelastically. $\frac{5}{6}$th of the initial kinetic energy is lost in whole process. What is value of M/m ? 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As in elastic or inelastic collision, momentum is conserved.

$\therefore$   $P_{i} = P_{f}$ 

$P_{i} =$ Initial momentum 

$P_{f} =$ Final Momentum 

      $mv = (2m + M) V_{f}$

$\Rightarrow$   $V_{f} =$ $\frac{mv}{2m+M}$

Here due to collision $\frac{5}{6}$th of kinetic energy is lost.

$\therefore$    Remaining kinetic energy, 

      $K_{f} =$ $\frac{1}{6}$ Ki

$\Rightarrow$    $\frac{1}{2}$(2m + M) $\times$ $\frac{(mv)^{2}}{(2m+M)^{2}}$ = $\frac{1}{6}\times \frac{1}{2}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{m^{2}v^{2}}{2m+M}$ = $\frac{1}{6}mv^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{m}{2m+M}$ = $\frac{1}{6}$

$\Rightarrow$   6m = 2m + M

$\Rightarrow$   M = 4m

$\Rightarrow$    $\frac{M}{m}$ = 4

text:
A particle is moving with a velocity

$\vec{v}\quad =K(y\hat{i}+x\hat{j}),$ where K is a constant. 

The general equation for its path is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given,

$\vec{v}=K\left (y\hat{i}+x\hat{j}\right )$

$\therefore$   Velocity in x direction, 

$v_{x}=\frac{dx}{dt}=Ky$   . . . . . (1)

Velocity in y direction, 

$v_{y} =$ $\frac{dy}{dt}$ = Kx . . . . . . . (2)

$\therefore$   $\frac{\frac{dy}{dt}}{\frac{dx}{dt}}=\frac{Kx}{Ky}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{x}{y}$

$\Rightarrow$   ydy $=$ xdx

Integrating both sides we get, 

$\int ydy=\int xdx$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{y^{2}}{2}=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+c$

$\Rightarrow$   $y^{2}=x^{2}+2c$

$\therefore$   General equation, 

$y^{2} = x^{2} +$ constant.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
An infinitely long current carrying wire and a small current carrying loop are in the plane of the paper as shown. The radius of the loop is a and distance of its centre from the wire is d (d > > a).  If the loop applies a force F on the wire then : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Magnetic field due to current carrying loop at distance d, is, 

B  =  $\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\times \frac{\vec{M}\times \vec{d}}{d^{3}}$

=  $\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\times \frac{i\times πa^{2}\times d\times \sin 90^{o}}{d^{3}}$   [as  M = iA]

=  $\frac{μ_{0}}{4π}\times \frac{iπa^{2}}{d^{2}}$

$\therefore$   B $\propto$ $\frac{a^{2}}{d^{2}}$ 

We also know, 

F = Bil

$\therefore$   F $\propto$  B

So, F $\propto$  $\frac{a^{2}}{d^{2}}$

text: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency 50 MHz travels in free space along the  positive x-direction. At a particular point in space and time, $\vec{E}=6.3\hat{j}V/m.$ The corresponding magnetic field $\vec{B,}$ at that point will be :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Given, $\vec{E}=6.3\hat{j}$

$\therefore$   $\left |\vec{E}\right |=\sqrt{(6.3)^{2}}=6.3$

$\therefore$   $\left |\vec{B}\right |=\frac{\left |\vec{E}\right |}{C}$

$=\frac{6.3}{3\times 10^{8}}$

$=2.1\times 10^{-8}$ T

Now we have to find the direction of $\vec{B}$.

We know, $\widehat{E}\times \widehat{B}=\widehat{C}$ and given $\vec{E}$ is in y-direction and wave moving in positive x-direction.

$\therefore$   $\widehat{J}\times \widehat{B}=\hat{i}$

$\Rightarrow$   $\widehat{B}=\widehat{K}$

$\therefore$   $\vec{B}=\left |\vec{B}\right |\widehat{B}$

$=2.1\times 10^{-8}\widehat{K}T$

text: A rod, of length L at room temperature and uniform area of cross section A, is made of a metal having coefficient of linear expansion $α/^{o}C$. It is observed that an external compressive force F, is applied on each of its ends, prevents any change in the length of the rod, when its temperature rises by $\Delta$T K. Young's modulus, Y, for this metal is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
We know,  

Young's Modulus, Y = $\frac{Stress}{Strain}$

Stress = $\frac{F}{A}$

Strain = $\frac{\Delta l}{l}$

$\therefore$  Y =  $\frac{\frac{F}{A}}{\frac{\Delta l}{l}}$

We also know, 

$l_{f}$ = $l_{i}$ (1 + $α\Delta$T)

$\Rightarrow$   $l_{f}$  =  $l_{i}$  +  $l_{i}α\Delta$T

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{l_{f}-l_{i}}{l_{i}}$  =  $α\Delta T$

$\Rightarrow$   $\frac{\Delta l}{l_{i}}$ = $α\Delta$T

$\therefore$   y  =  $\frac{\frac{F}{A}}{α\Delta T}$

=  $\frac{F}{Aα\Delta T}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
A gas can be taken from A to B via two different processes ACB and ADB. 


[IMG]


When path ACB is used 60 J of heat flows into the system and 30 J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used work done by the system is 10 J. The heat Flow into the system in path ADB is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Using law of thermodynamics in path ACB, 

$\Delta Q_{$ACB} = $\Delta U_{$ACB} + $\Delta W_{$ACB}

$\Rightarrow$   60  =  $\Delta U_{$ACB} + 30

$\Rightarrow$   $\Delta U_{$ACB} = 30 J

As value of $\Delta$U is path independent, 

$\therefore$   $\Delta U_{$ACB} = $\Delta U_{$ADB}  =  30 J

$\therefore$   In path ADB,

$\Delta Q_{$ADB} = $\Delta U_{$ADB} + $\Delta W_{$ADB}

$\Rightarrow\Delta Q_{$ADB} = 30 + 10 = 40 J
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot

text:
A parallel plate capacitor is made of two square plates of side 'a', separated by a distance d (d < < a). The lower triangular portion is filled with a dielectric of dielectric constant K, as shown in the figure. Capacitance of this capacitor is : 


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Take a strip of the plates at distance $x$ from the thin edge of the dielectric, of width $dx$ and length $a$ (area $adx$). In this strip the dielectric has thickness $y=\dfrac{d}{a}x$ and the air gap is $d-y$.

The air layer and the dielectric layer of the strip are in series:

$dC=\dfrac{ε_{0}adx}{(d-y)+\dfrac{y}{K}}=\dfrac{ε_{0}adx}{d-βx},β=\dfrac{d}{a}\left (1-\dfrac{1}{K}\right )=\dfrac{d(K-1)}{aK}$

All strips connect the same two plates, so they are in parallel and their capacitances add:

$C=\int\limits _{0}^{a}\dfrac{ε_{0}adx}{d-βx}=\dfrac{ε_{0}a}{β}\ln \dfrac{d}{d-βa}$

At $x=a$, $d-βa=d-\dfrac{d(K-1)}{K}=\dfrac{d}{K}$, so the logarithm equals $\ln K$:

$C=\dfrac{ε_{0}a\cdot aK}{d(K-1)}\ln K=\dfrac{Kε_{0}a^{2}}{d(K-1)}\ln K$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text: Drift speed of electrons, when 1.5 A of current flows in a copper wire of cross section $5 mm^{2}$, is $υ$. If the electron density in copper is 9 $\times$ $10^{28}/m^{3}$ the value of $υ$. in mm/s is close to (Take charge of electron to be = 1.6 $\times$ $10^{-19}C)$

solution.body:
We know, 

I = neAV$_{d}$

$\therefore$   $V_{d} =$ $\frac{\mathrm{I}}{neA}$

=   $\frac{1.5}{9\times 10^{28}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 5\times 10^{-6}}$

=   0.02 m/s

text: Mobility of electrons in a semiconductor is defined as the ratio of their drift velocity to the applied electric field. If, for an n-type semiconductor, the density of electrons is $10^{19} m^{-3}$ and their mobility is $1.6 m^{2}/(V.s)$ then the resistivity of the semiconductor (since it is an n-type semiconductor contribution of holes is ignored) is close to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
For semiconductor, 

Conductivity, $σ$ $= n_{e} q$ $μ_{e}$ $+ n_{h} q$ $μ_{h}$

given that semiconductor is n-type. So contribution of holes is ignored.

$\therefore$   $n_{h} q$ $μ_{h}$ = 0

$\therefore$   $σ$ $= n_{e} q$ $μ_{e}$

Resistivity, $ρ$ = $\frac{1}{σ}$

=  $\frac{1}{n_{e}qμ_{e}}$

=  $\frac{1}{10^{19}\times 1.6\times 10^{-19}\times 1.6}$

=  $\frac{1}{1.6\times 1.6}$

=  0.4 $\Omega$ m

text: A bar magnet is demagnetized by inserting it inside a solenoid of length 0.2 m, 100 turns, and carrying a current of 5.2 A. The coercivity of the bar magnet is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 9th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Coercivity, H = $\frac{B}{μ_{0}}$

Inside solenoid the magnetic field, 

B  = $μ_{0}$ni

$\therefore$   H = $\frac{μ_{0}ni}{μ_{0}}$

=  ni

= $\frac{N}{\ell }\times i$

=  $\frac{100}{0.2}\times 5.2$

= 2600 A/m
